o: not paid for by the firm that benefits
always shown on television at night
controlled entirely by the firm's own staff
questions.e: Publicity, such as a news report about a firm, is free and not controlled by the firm. Advertising is paid for, and the firm controls the message.

questions.s: Free samples, discount coupons and prize contests are tools of
questions.e: Sales promotion offers short-term incentives to encourage immediate buying. Personal selling is face-to-face persuasion by a salesman.

questions.s: Advertising by letters, leaflets or catalogues sent to selected people's addresses is
questions.e: Direct mail reaches chosen individuals by post with personal material. Outdoor advertising uses billboards and signs in public places.

questions.s: The process of collecting and analysing information about consumers, competitors and markets to guide marketing decisions is
questions.e: Market research studies buyers' needs and market conditions before decisions are taken. Sales promotion uses incentives to push current sales.

questions.s: In Pakistan, the stock exchange that was formed in 2016 by merging the Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad exchanges is the
questions.e: The three exchanges merged in January 2016 to form the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX). The State Bank is the central bank and has no role as an exchange.

questions.s: A stock exchange is best described as
o: a bank that lends money to listed companies only
a market where companies sell their manufactured goods directly to consumers
an organised market for buying and selling existing securities
a government office that registers new companies
questions.e: A stock exchange provides a regulated place where shares, bonds and other securities already issued can be traded. Registering companies is the work of the SECP's company registry.

questions.s: A speculator who buys shares expecting their prices to rise, so as to sell later at a profit, is called a
questions.e: A bull expects a rise and buys now; a bear expects a fall and sells now hoping to buy back cheaper. A rising market is called a bull market.

questions.s: A speculator who sells shares expecting a fall in their prices is a
questions.e: A bear sells now in the hope of buying back later at a lower price. A broker simply buys and sells on behalf of clients for commission.

questions.s: A person who applies for newly issued shares, not to keep them, but to sell them quickly at a premium once trading begins is a
questions.e: A stag deals in new issues, hoping to profit from the rise in price soon after listing. A lame duck is a bear who cannot meet his commitments.

questions.s: A bear speculator who is unable to meet his commitments on the settlement day is called a
questions.e: When prices rise instead of falling, a bear who has sold shares he does not own may be unable to deliver them; he is then a lame duck. A stag deals in new issues.

questions.s: The market in which a company sells new shares to investors for the first time is the
questions.e: New issues, such as an initial public offering, are sold in the primary market, and the company receives the money. Later trading between investors on the exchange is the secondary market.

questions.s: Securities of companies that have been admitted to trading on a stock exchange are called
questions.e: A company's shares are listed when the exchange admits them for trading after the company meets its rules. Unlisted securities are not traded on the exchange.

questions.s: The main purpose of an office is to
o: receive, record, arrange and supply information
manufacture goods for sale in local and foreign markets
questions.e: An office handles the information a business needs: it receives and records data, arranges it and supplies it to managers. Manufacturing takes place in a factory.

questions.s: Numerical filing usually requires
o: no index at all, because numbers are easy to remember
files to be kept in order of their dates
files to be arranged first by provinces and then by districts and cities
a separate index to find the number given to each correspondent
questions.e: Each correspondent is given a number, so a card index of names with their numbers is needed to locate a file. Arrangement by area is geographical filing.

questions.s: A firm with branches all over Pakistan arranges its files by provinces and then by cities. This is
questions.e: Geographical filing groups papers by location, which suits firms whose work is organised by sales areas. Within each area, files may then be arranged alphabetically.

questions.s: In centralised filing,
o: records are sent to customers and suppliers for safe keeping in their own offices
all the records of the organisation are kept in one filing department
each department keeps its own files separately
files are kept by each employee at his desk
questions.e: Centralised filing places all files under one section with trained staff and uniform methods. Each department keeping its own files is decentralised filing.

questions.s: A machine used in offices to print postage on letters instead of sticking stamps is a
questions.e: A franking machine prints the postage value and date on envelopes, and the post office is paid in advance. A shredder cuts confidential papers into strips.

questions.s: In an office, all letters received are first entered in the
questions.e: The inward (incoming) mail register records date, sender and subject of each letter received, and the department it is sent to. The outward register records letters sent out.

questions.s: A book signed by the receiver of letters delivered by hand, as proof of delivery, is the
questions.e: The peon (messenger) book records letters delivered by hand, and the receiver signs it. The minute book records the proceedings of meetings.

questions.s: Communication from managers to their subordinates, such as instructions and orders, is
questions.e: Downward communication flows from higher to lower levels of authority. Reports and suggestions from workers to managers are upward communication.

questions.s: The informal, unofficial network through which rumours spread in an organisation is called the
questions.e: The grapevine carries information outside official channels; it is fast but often inaccurate. The chain of command is the formal line of authority.

questions.s: A short written message used for communication between departments within the same organisation is a
questions.e: A memorandum (memo) is an internal note with headings such as To, From, Date and Subject, and no salutation or complimentary close. A press release is sent outside to the media.

questions.s: A business letter begins "Dear Sir". The matching complimentary close in British usage is
questions.e: In British convention, "Dear Sir" or "Dear Madam" is followed by "Yours faithfully", while a letter to a named person such as "Dear Mr Raza" ends "Yours sincerely".

questions.s: A letter written by a firm to a bank or another trader to ask about the financial standing of a new customer is a
questions.e: A status enquiry asks a referee whether a prospective customer is creditworthy, and replies are treated as confidential. A collection letter asks a customer to pay an overdue account.

questions.s: The section of a business letter that briefly states what the letter is about, placed after the salutation, is the
questions.e: The subject line, such as "Subject: Order No. 245", tells the reader at once what the letter concerns. The inside address gives the name and address of the receiver.

questions.s: The list of items of business to be discussed at a meeting, sent to members in advance, is the
questions.e: The agenda sets out the order of business for the meeting. Minutes are the official record written after the meeting of what was discussed and decided.

questions.s: Which of the following is an example of a barrier to communication?
o: choosing a channel of communication that suits both the message and the receiver
use of technical words the receiver does not understand
using short, clear sentences in a letter
giving feedback to show the message was understood
questions.e: Unfamiliar jargon stops the receiver from decoding the message, so it is a semantic barrier. Feedback, a suitable channel and clear sentences all help communication.

questions.s: A letter written by a buyer to a supplier to ask for prices, terms and samples of goods is a
questions.e: A letter of enquiry asks for information before buying; the supplier's reply is usually a quotation. A letter of complaint is written after a problem with goods or services.

questions.s: A seller replies to a customer's complaint about damaged goods, offering to replace them. Such a reply is a
questions.e: A letter of adjustment answers a complaint and states how it will be settled, such as by replacement, repair or a credit note. A circular letter is a single message sent to many readers.

questions.s: A letter sent to many customers at once to announce, for example, the opening of a new branch is a
questions.e: A circular letter carries the same message to a large number of people. A letter of adjustment answers one particular customer's complaint.

questions.s: In a business letter, the name and address of the person to whom the letter is written, placed above the salutation, is the
questions.e: The inside address identifies the receiver. The letterhead, printed at the top, carries the sender's own name, address and contact details.

questions.s: A good business letter is "concise" when it
o: uses long, formal sentences to sound impressive
says what is needed in as few words as clarity allows
leaves out important details to save the writer's time
is written entirely in capital letters for emphasis
questions.e: Conciseness means removing unnecessary words while keeping all the facts the reader needs. Leaving out important details makes a letter incomplete, which is a different fault.

questions.s: Communication by facial expressions, gestures and body posture is
questions.e: Non-verbal communication sends messages without words. Written communication uses words on paper or a screen.

questions.s: A file in which loose papers are kept in a cardboard box with a spring clip, often used for current correspondence, is a
questions.e: A box file holds papers flat under a spring clip and is easy to store on shelves. A card index stores information on separate cards in a drawer.

questions.s: The process of preparing a guide to the contents of files, so that papers can be located quickly, is
questions.e: An index, such as a card index of names and file numbers, points the user to the right file. Franking prints postage, and auditing checks accounts.

questions.s: Which of the following is the best reason for a firm to use a microfilm or digital record of old documents?
o: avoiding the need for any index or filing system
saving storage space while keeping records available
making the records impossible for staff to read
increasing the number of paper files kept in every department of the office
questions.e: Microfilming or scanning reduces bulky paper to compact form that can still be retrieved. It does not remove the need for an index; digital files must still be organised.

questions.s: The price of a company's share quoted on the stock exchange is its
questions.e: The market value is what buyers pay on the exchange and changes daily. Face (par) value is the amount printed on the share certificate and does not change with trading.

questions.s: To send a copy of a business e-mail to a person without the other recipients seeing that person's address, the sender enters it in the
questions.e: Bcc (blind carbon copy) hides that address from the other recipients. Addresses in the Cc field are visible to everyone who receives the message.

questions.s: The element of the marketing mix that covers advertising and sales promotion is
questions.e: Promotion includes all ways of communicating with buyers: advertising, personal selling, sales promotion and publicity. Place is about distribution.

questions.s: Pricing a new product high at launch, to earn more from buyers willing to pay more, and lowering it later is
questions.e: Skimming takes the "cream" of the market first with a high price. Penetration pricing starts low to win many buyers fast.

questions.s: Billboards and neon signs beside roads are examples of
questions.e: Outdoor advertising reaches people in public places. Press advertising appears in newspapers and magazines.

questions.s: A person who buys and sells shares on the stock exchange on behalf of clients for a commission is a
questions.e: A broker is an agent of investors and earns commission. Bulls, bears and stags are types of speculators who trade on their own account.

questions.s: The regulator of the stock market in Pakistan is the
o: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
questions.e: The SECP regulates the stock exchange, brokers and listed companies. The State Bank regulates banks and monetary policy.

questions.s: Arranging papers in order of their dates is
questions.e: Chronological filing places papers in date order, often within another arrangement. Alphabetical filing follows names.

questions.s: Communication between managers at the same level, such as the sales and production managers, is
questions.e: Horizontal (lateral) communication flows between people at the same level to coordinate work. Downward communication goes from superiors to subordinates.

questions.s: A letter to a named person beginning "Dear Ms Ayesha" usually ends with
questions.e: In British usage, a letter with a personal salutation ends "Yours sincerely". "Yours faithfully" is used when the salutation is "Dear Sir" or "Dear Madam".

questions.s: A letter sent to a customer reminding him to pay an overdue account is a
questions.e: Collection letters ask politely, then firmly, for payment of amounts due. A letter of enquiry asks for information before buying.

questions.s: An office machine that cuts unwanted confidential papers into thin strips is a
questions.e: A shredder destroys confidential documents so they cannot be read. A photocopier makes copies of documents.

questions.s: In the product life cycle, a firm is most likely to cut prices sharply and stop advertising a product in the
questions.e: In decline, sales and profits fall as tastes change or new products appear, so firms cut costs and may withdraw the product. Heavy promotion is typical of the introduction stage.

questions.s: Which of the following is a function of a stock exchange?
o: printing currency notes for the government
providing liquidity by letting investors sell securities easily
registering new companies and keeping their memorandum and articles on record
fixing the dividend that companies must pay
questions.e: A stock exchange gives investors a ready market, so they can turn shares into cash, and it helps value securities. Registering companies is done by the SECP, and dividends are decided by each company.

questions.s: Filing means
o: typing letters to customers and suppliers
destroying old letters and records each year
arranging and keeping records so that they can be found quickly
sending all outward letters to customers by post or by courier service
questions.e: Filing preserves documents in an orderly way so they can be traced when needed. Destroying records is not filing, though old records are reviewed under a retention policy.

questions.s: Arranging files according to the first letters of names of customers or suppliers is
questions.e: Alphabetical filing follows the A-Z order of names and is the simplest and most common method. Chronological filing arranges papers by date.

questions.s: The written official record of the proceedings and decisions of a meeting is called the
questions.e: Minutes record who attended, what was discussed and what was resolved, and are signed by the chairman. A notice informs members of the date, time and place of a meeting.
